ags.name: AGS
ags.type: AI card grading with laser scanning
ags.what: A grading company that grades by machine. Each card is laser-scanned in under 10 seconds, roughly 30 million data points, and gets a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision, eight subgrades (centering, corners, edges and surface, front and back), a 3D heightmap and a digital report tied to its cert number. Cards are sealed in tamper-evident, ultrasonically welded slabs.
ags.fit: Collectors, sellers and card shops who want the same card to get the same grade every time, want to see why it got that grade, and want it back in weeks.
ags.pricing: $18 per card, flat, whatever the card is worth. Bulk tiers from 30 cards for TCG: $15 at 20 business days, $20 at 10, $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier. Return shipping is added at checkout. Code AGSNEW20 takes 20% off a first order.
ags.minimum: No minimum submission. Bulk pricing starts at 30 cards. You pay when the cards are graded and ready to ship.
ags.custody: Laser-scanned, graded by machine, eight subgrades, slabbed, back in 20 business days or less.
ags.lacks: A younger slab. PSA holders still bring the highest resale prices on most cards. Standard-size cards only.
ags.entry: $18 flat, or $15 in bulk (30+ TCG cards)
ags.fast: 5 business days at $30; same-day by request
ags.method: Machine: 3D laser scan, graded by algorithm

psa.name: PSA
psa.what: The largest card grader by volume and part of Collectors. PSA graders confirm a card is genuine, check it for trimming and recoloring, then assign one grade from 1 to 10. Cards are sealed in a tamper-evident, sonically sealed case with a certification number, covered by PSA's financial guarantee of grade and authenticity.
psa.fit: Sellers who want the widest buyer pool and the strongest resale prices, especially on high-value and vintage cards.
psa.pricing: Priced by service level and declared value. PSA's February 2026 update lists Value Bulk at $24.99 (Collectors Club members only), Value at $32.99, Value Plus at $49.99 with a 45 business day estimate, and Regular at $79.99 at 25. Open tiers changed during 2026, so check PSA's site before you ship.
psa.lacks: One overall grade with no subgrades. Long waits at the lower tiers, and fees that rise with the card's declared value.
psa.speed: 25 to 45+ business days on listed tiers
psa.fast: Express tiers, priced by declared value

bgs.name: BGS (Beckett)
bgs.what: Beckett Grading Services grades on a half-point scale and can print four subgrades on the label: centering, corners, edges and surface. Every card is checked for trimming and alteration first. Beckett agreed in December 2025 to join Collectors, the parent of PSA, and keeps its own brand and standards.
bgs.fit: Collectors who want subgrades printed on the label from one of the oldest names in the hobby.
bgs.pricing: Base $14.95 per card at 45+ business days ($17.95 with subgrades). Standard $34.95 at 20 to 25 days. Express $79.95 at 7 to 10. Priority $124.95 at 2 to 3. No minimums and no fees tied to card value. Autographed cards add $5.
bgs.lacks: Subgrades come from a grader's eye, with no measured report behind them. The Base tier takes 45 business days or more.

cgc.name: CGC Cards
cgc.type: Human-graded card grading, outside the Collectors group
cgc.what: The card arm of Certified Collectibles Group, which also grades comics, coins and paper money. CGC grades TCG, sports and non-sports cards and offers crossover from other holders, reholder, pedigree labels and autograph authentication.
cgc.fit: TCG collectors and volume submitters who want a low per-card price from a large grader that Collectors does not own.
cgc.pricing: Bulk $10 per card (10-card minimum, cards worth up to $500, 25 working days). Economy $13 (up to $1,000, 25 days). Standard $30 (up to $3,000, 15 days). Express $50 (up to $10,000, 5 days). Paid members save 10% to 20%. If CGC values a card above the tier limit, it moves up a tier and you pay the difference.
cgc.lacks: Tiers are capped by card value, so a strong card costs more to grade. No measured report behind the grade.
cgc.speed: 25 working days at Bulk and Economy
cgc.upcharge: Yes, tiers capped by card value
cgc.subgrades: Not listed on the fee page

sgc.name: SGC
sgc.type: Human-graded card grading, known for vintage
sgc.what: A long-running grader, owned by Collectors since 2024, best known for vintage sports cards and its black-insert holder. SGC prices by the card's declared value.
sgc.fit: Vintage sports card collectors who like the holder and its standing with pre-war cards.
sgc.pricing: Sports Collectors Daily reported that SGC raised its base price from $15 to $50 per card in September 2026. Faster service costs more and scales with declared value. Check SGC's site for the tiers open now.
sgc.lacks: No longer a budget pick after the 2026 price change. A smaller buyer pool for modern TCG cards.
sgc.source_note: SGC's pricing page blocked automated reading on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-18. The price is as reported by Sports Collectors Daily and SI. Recheck by hand.

tag.name: TAG Grading
tag.what: TAG grades with imaging technology it describes as multi-patented, checked by its experts. Each slab links by QR code to a DIG report that maps the card's defects, and higher tiers add a 1000-point score ranked against every card TAG has graded. Slabs are clear acrylic with the card ID inscribed in the slab and no paper label.
tag.fit: Collectors who want a technology-assisted grade with a defect report and a 1000-point score.
tag.pricing: No upcharge for card value. TAG's pricing page showed no per-card prices on November 18, 2026, under a limited reopening banner. Check TAG for the tiers and prices open now.
tag.lacks: Does not accept pre-1989 cards, Yu-Gi-Oh!, memorabilia cards or stock thicker than 50pt. Capacity was limited for much of 2026.
tag.subgrades: Defect report; 1000-point score on higher tiers

isa.name: ISA Grading
isa.type: Human-graded card grading at one flat price
isa.what: International Sports Authentication, based in Brighton, Michigan. ISA grades sports cards, TCG cards and vintage at one flat rate and seals them in tamper-evident slabs with a serial number that can be checked on its site.
isa.fit: Collectors who want one flat price and a two-week turnaround without picking a tier.
isa.pricing: $15 per card, flat, with a 10-card minimum and a 14-day turnaround. ISA says it adds no upcharges.
isa.lacks: A small buyer pool. ISA slabs sell for less than the big names on most cards.

gma.name: GMA Grading
gma.what: A budget grader for sports and non-sports cards. GMA sells three tiers by speed and drops the price again on orders of 100 cards or more.
gma.fit: Sellers slabbing low-value cards in volume, where the grading fee has to stay near $10.
gma.pricing: Economy $12 per card (25-card minimum, 25 business days), $9 at 100 or more. Standard $15 (20-card minimum, 15 days). Gold Express $25 (10-card minimum, 10 days).
gma.lacks: GMA slabs carry little resale premium. Every tier has a minimum order.

ace.name: Ace Grading
ace.what: A British grader popular with TCG collectors in the UK and Europe. Ace prices in pounds across five service levels and sells optional custom labels.
ace.fit: Collectors in the UK and Europe who want a local grader and no customs paperwork.
ace.pricing: Per card: Basic £12, Standard £15, Premier £18, Ultra £25, Luxury £50, as listed in Ace's help center. Labels and shipping are extra.
ace.lacks: Little recognition among US buyers, so resale outside the UK and Europe is thin.

arena.name: Arena Club
arena.type: AI-assisted card grading with a vault and marketplace
arena.what: Arena Club grades with expert graders working alongside computer vision and AI, with three rounds of review before slabbing. Cards get four subgrades, an ultrasonically welded slab and a QR code that opens a grading report. Graded cards can go straight into its insured vault and app marketplace.
arena.fit: Collectors who want to grade, vault and sell inside one app.
arena.pricing: Arena Club's grading page lists no per-card price. Check the Arena Club app or site for current pricing.
arena.lacks: The slab is tied to Arena Club's own marketplace and has a thin record elsewhere.
arena.entry: Not listed on the grading page
